description: Simit is a beloved Turkish bread, often called a Turkish bagel, known for its distinct ring shape and generous coating of toasted sesame seeds. This iconic street food boasts a delightfully chewy interior and a crisp, nutty exterior, making it a perfect companion for breakfast or a snack. Enjoy the taste of Turkey with this authentic homemade Simit recipe.

ingredients.notes: grape molasses or pekmez is preferred

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the warm water, sugar, and active dry yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: Add the flour, salt, and olive oil to the yeast mixture. Mix with a spoon until a shaggy dough forms. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until it is smooth and elastic. The dough should be soft and slightly tacky.

instructions.title: First Rise
instructions.text: Place the kneaded dough in a lightly oiled bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until it has doubled in size.

instructions.title: Shape the Simits
instructions.text: Punch down the risen dough and divide it into 8 equal pieces. Roll each piece into a long rope, approximately 18-20 inches (45-50 cm) long. Twist two ropes together, then connect the ends to form a ring. Repeat with the remaining dough pieces.

instructions.title: Prepare Molasses Dip and Sesame Coating
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 400F (200C). In a shallow dish, whisk together the molasses and 1/2 cup water. In another shallow dish, spread out the sesame seeds. Dip each simit first into the molasses mixture, ensuring it is fully coated, then immediately transfer it to the sesame seeds, pressing gently to adhere a generous amount of seeds on all sides.

instructions.title: Bake the Simits
instructions.text: Place the coated simits on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving some space between them. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until they are deeply golden brown and crispy. Allow to cool slightly on a wire rack before serving.

tips: For the most authentic flavor, use grape molasses (pekmez) in your dip. It provides a unique depth of flavor and a beautiful dark crust.
Ensure your sesame seeds are fresh and, if desired, lightly toasted in a dry pan before coating. This enhances their nutty aroma and flavor.

Simit is best enjoyed fresh and warm. If you have leftovers, store them at room temperature in an airtight container for up to two days. Reheat briefly in a toaster or oven to restore their crispness.
